compiled_state.title: [CHRONIC sync — manually mirrored from Jira while inbound bridge inoperative] Jira bridge sync remediation: parent, tags, link relations (DIG-1939)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

The Jira bridge (`plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/`) tracks only four fields in EDIT events: `priority`, `assignee`, `title`, `description` (see `_handle_edit.py:73-88`). Three DSO-local fields with direct Jira analogs are never synced: `parent_id` (Jira Epic Link), `tags` (Jira Labels), and `blocks`/`depends_on` link relations (Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks"). This leads to silent divergence where a local reparent or retag is invisible in Jira, and vice versa. Additionally, the new `supersedes` relation (scoped in Epic 6f7a-4ba6 expansion) must sync lossily as Jira "Relates" with a local-richer-wins precedence rule on inbound. This epic closes all four bridge sync gaps in one coherent remediation.

## Success Criteria
- `parent_id` synced bidirectionally via Jira Epic Link field. Outbound: local parent-child changes write the Epic Link on next sync. Inbound: Jira Epic Link changes write a local EDIT(parent_id) event. Reducer EDIT handler extended.
- `tags` synced bidirectionally via Jira Labels. Outbound: tag add/remove writes Jira label update. Inbound: Jira label change writes local EDIT(tags) event.
- `blocks` and `depends_on` link relations synced bidirectionally via Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks". Outbound: new LINK event triggers Jira issue-link create. Inbound: new Jira Issue Link triggers local LINK event. UNLINK symmetric.
- `supersedes` relation synced lossily as Jira "Relates" (no native Jira supersedes type). Local `supersedes` value is authoritative: on inbound, if a Jira "Relates" link matches an existing local `supersedes`, local wins; other "Relates" links are imported as local `relates_to`.
- Bridge EDIT event tracking extended in `_handle_edit.py` from 4 fields to 7 (adding parent_id, tags, link-deltas). Comprehensive integration tests covering all four sync directions pass.
- Conflict handling: on simultaneous local + remote change to the same field, bridge raises BRIDGE_ALERT for human resolution (existing pattern).

## Approach
Extend `_handle_edit.py` to track `parent_id`, `tags`, and link-deltas in EDIT tracking. Extend `_outbound_handlers.py` to write Jira Epic Link, Labels, and Issue Links. Extend `_inbound_api.py` to read these Jira fields and emit local EDIT/LINK events. Add precedence rule for `supersedes`-over-`relates` in link handler. Coordinate with Epic 6f7a-4ba6 to ensure `supersedes` relation exists before this epics supersedes-sync work lands.

## Dependencies
- Depends on Epic 1de7-50d4 (resolution/reporter — reducer schema prerequisite for clean EDIT event extension).
- Serialized after Epic 6f7a-4ba6 (extended `ticket link` for `supersedes` relation must exist before this epic can sync it). Overlaps bridge files with 6f7a-4ba6 expansion.

## Out of Scope
- Jira custom field mapping beyond parent/labels/links
- Agent-specific Jira accountId provisioning
- Jira permission escalation handling (operational concern)

---
## Chronic Issue Context
Maps to Jira DIG-1939 (Priority: High, Status: To Do). Manually mirrored — inbound bridge inoperative.

comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND (debug-everything 2026-05-08)

Both Inbound Bridge and Outbound Bridge GitHub Actions workflows have been failing on **every scheduled run** (100% failure rate, every 30-60 min for at least the past day). The failure is at the very first step:

```
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
ERROR: BRIDGE_ENV_ID is unset or empty — cannot run outbound bridge.
```

**Root cause**: The `BRIDGE_ENV_ID` repo variable is **not set** in this repository (verified via `gh variable list` — variable is absent). Per CLAUDE.md architecture: 'BRIDGE_ENV_ID required UUID repo variable; bridges fail-fast when empty.'

**Effect**: No outbound writes have reached Jira; no inbound updates have reached the local tracker. Every chronic sync ticket downstream of this gate (DIG-1845, DIG-1939, DIG-1688, DIG-1999, DIG-1995, DIG-2003, DIG-2002, DIG-2001) is observed-broken because the bridge never executes its actual sync logic.

**Fix command** (requires repo-admin authorization — DO NOT execute autonomously):

```
gh variable set BRIDGE_ENV_ID --body 'c3d2c46e-df9e-40c4-8014-5e8c9fdf3cc1'
```

The canonical env_id is taken from existing local tickets (verified across 1348-f163, 60a8-d9ad, etc.). Setting it must match — using a freshly-generated UUID would orphan all existing local tickets from any future bridge sync.

**Evidence run IDs**:
- Outbound (latest 10 failures): 25564610760, 25561828571, 25558743524, ...
- Inbound  (latest 10 failures): 25564432014, 25561633684, 25558602451, ...

**Recommended next steps after BRIDGE_ENV_ID is set**:
1. Trigger a backfill: `gh workflow run outbound-bridge.yml -f backfill=true`
2. Validate first run completes past Validate step (no longer exits 1)
3. Then DIG-1688's CalledProcessError will surface as the next failure mode (per its description) — that one is a real code bug to fix.
4. Then DIG-1999's assignee gap; then DIG-1939's parent/tags/links coverage gap.

comments.body:
## CORRECTION + RESOLUTION (2026-05-08, same session)

Initial fix used local env_id as BRIDGE_ENV_ID — that was **wrong**. Per plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/README.md: BRIDGE_ENV_ID identifies the *bridge instance* and is used by **inbound for echo prevention**. If it equals local tickets' env_id, inbound treats every Jira event as an echo and never imports anything (would have only fixed outbound, kept inbound silently broken).

**Corrected**: BRIDGE_ENV_ID set to a fresh CI-bridge-unique UUID 87bd1065-0264-4126-94b7-ae8c71b8d506, distinct from local env_id c3d2c46e-…

**Verified outcome**:
- Outbound run 25565196684: SUCCESS
- Inbound  run 25565198050: SUCCESS
- 10/10 prior runs: failure (BRIDGE_ENV_ID unset)

The umbrella sync gate is fixed. Downstream specific bugs (DIG-1688 acli delete CalledProcessError, DIG-1999 assignee fallback, DIG-1939 parent/tags/links) remain — they will surface in subsequent run logs as the bridge now actually executes its sync logic.

Filed companion bug 7273-997c-9c4d-4e50 (P1) for the operational silent-failure: 100% bridge failure rate persisted ≥1 day with no operator alerting — needs failure-streak detection / Slack notification / dso:tickets-health surfacing.
